## Part A — Creating Vectors and List:
```{r}
#Question 1
# a. Create a vector for the worker's age.
worker_age <- c(34, 28, 22, 36, 27, 18, 52, 39, 42, 29, 35, 31, 27, 22, 37, 34, 19, 20, 57, 49, 50, 37, 46, 25, 17, 37, 43, 53, 41, 51, 35, 24, 33, 41, 53, 40, 18, 44, 38, 41, 48, 27, 39, 19, 30, 61, 54, 58, 26, 18)

# b. How many data points?
length(worker_age)

# c. Find the minimum and the maximum value of worker's age.
min(worker_age)
max(worker_age)

# d. Access the 13th to 18th elements and 33th to 35th elements of worker's age.
worker_age[c(13:18, 33:35)]

# e. Access all but the 10th, 20th, 30th and 40th elements.
worker_age[-c(10, 20, 30, 40)]

# f. Modify the 4th, 14th, 24th, and 44th elements with value = 0.
worker_age[c(4, 14, 24, 44)] <- 0

#Question 2
data(rivers)

# Compute statistics
river_stats <- c(
  Count = length(rivers),
  Sum = sum(rivers),
  Mean = mean(rivers),
  Median = median(rivers),
  Variance = var(rivers),
  StdDev = sd(rivers),
  Min = min(rivers),
  Max = max(rivers)
)

river_stats

#Question 3
# Create vectors for Forbes data (example sample vectors based on top attributes)
celeb_name <- c("Oprah Winfrey", "Tiger Woods", "Madonna", "Tom Cruise", "Steven Spielberg")
power_ranking <- c(1, 2, 3, 4, 5)
pay_annual <- c(225, 87, 40, 31, 200)

# Create data frame or named list representation
forbes_df <- data.frame(Name = celeb_name, PowerRank = power_ranking, Pay = pay_annual)

# Modify J.K. Rowling (or target row) power ranking to 15 and pay to 90

#Question 4
# a. Create a list of ten vegetables
vegetables <- list("Carrot", "Broccoli", "Spinach", "Potato", "Tomato", "Cabbage", "Lettuce", "Cucumber", "Eggplant", "Pumpkin")

# b. Add 2 additional vegetables after the last vegetables
vegetables <- append(vegetables, list("Zucchini", "Radish"))

# c. How many datapoints do you have?
length(vegetables)

# d. Add 4 additional vegetables after index 5
vegetables <- append(vegetables, list("Garlic", "Onion", "Peas", "Corn"), after = 5)

# e. How many datapoints does your vegetable list have now?
length(vegetables)
```
